items.q: A primary source of economic data is one where
o: the data are estimated by a model
the data are collected first hand for the study at hand
the data already exist in published reports
the data come from a textbook
items.s: Primary data are gathered directly by the investigator; secondary data already exist elsewhere.

items.q: A census differs from a sample survey because a census
o: covers every unit in the population
items.s: A census enumerates the whole population; a sample survey studies a part and infers about the whole.

items.q: The National Bureau of Statistics household survey is an example of
o: a primary source for every user
a secondary source when another researcher reuses it
items.s: Data collected by one body become secondary data in the hands of another researcher.

items.q: Non response bias arises when
o: the sample is drawn at random
those who fail to respond differ systematically from those who respond
items.s: Systematic differences between responders and non responders distort the estimate.

items.q: A questionnaire with leading questions suffers from
items.s: Leading wording pushes respondents towards a particular answer.

items.q: Continuous economic data are best collected by
o: measurement that can take any value in a range
items.s: Continuous variables such as income or output can take any value within a range.

items.q: Pilot testing a questionnaire before the main survey is done to
o: detect ambiguous wording and unusable questions
items.s: A pilot exposes faults in wording, ordering and coding before the real fieldwork.

items.q: The main advantage of secondary data is
o: the saving in time and cost of collection
freedom from out of date figures
items.s: Secondary data are cheaper and quicker, though definitions and vintage must be checked.

items.q: A sampling frame is
o: the questionnaire used in the field
the list of units from which the sample is drawn
items.s: Without an adequate frame the intended population cannot be sampled properly.

items.q: Data collected at one point in time across many units are called
items.s: Cross sectional data compare units at one time; time series follow one unit over time.
